was: Small private wooded campground at 40 US Route 7, Leicester. 41 sites; RV sites have water and 30-amp electric; pool, laundry, showers, dump station. Open May 1-Oct 14. Nightly plus weekly/monthly rates; reserve by phone (no online booking shown). Not on water - nearest lakes/river within ~5 miles. --Claude

was: Gilson Pond camping area at Monadnock SP: 41 sites total (16 tent-only, 12 platform, 5 RV/trailer up to 30 ft, 3 standard up to 25 ft, plus 5 remote hike-to). A 23-ft RV fits the RV/Trailer sites. No hookups per official reservation page. Flush toilets, showers, drinking water, small camp store. Season ~May 1-Oct 11. Reservable online/by phone via NH State Parks (ReserveAmerica). --Claude  Correction 2026-10-12: the booking site now lists 30-amp electric (no water or sewer) on the five RV/Trailer sites. --Claude

was: NH state park on White Lake (Tamworth/W. Ossipee). ~200 wooded sites across two camping areas; tents, trailers and RVs (12 tent-only sites). Communal water spigots; coin-op showers. Max RV ~38 ft but many sites smaller-check length when booking. Open Memorial Day weekend to ~mid-Oct; reservable via ReserveAmerica with some FCFS sites held. --Claude

was: Small 7-site state-run RV park at the Cannon Mountain tramway base on Echo Lake (Franconia Notch). Full 3-way hookups (water/sewer/electric) May-Columbus Day; off-season electric only, carry-in/carry-out. Self-contained rigs to 40 ft; reservations required year-round (ReserveAmerica); no pets. NOT the ski area-this is the adjacent RV park. --Claude

was: City of Keene Parks & Recreation municipal campground. 43 sites -- mix of full-hookup, water-only, electric-only and no-hookup (dry) sites; big-rig friendly up to ~40 ft. Dump station, swimming pool (fee, late June-Aug), hot showers, laundry, playground, ballfields. Open Memorial Day weekend through mid-September. Reservable online via RecDesk or by phone. --Claude

was: Owned and operated by the Hanover Improvement Society (private non-profit). 17 RV sites + 12 tent sites; RV sites big-rig friendly up to 50 ft with full or partial hookups; dump station, swimming pool, hot showers, laundry. Season mid-May through Columbus Day. Reservations strongly recommended -- book online at storrspond.org or call the office. --Claude

was: Family-owned since 1971; 50 wooded sites (RV sites 1-42 plus tent sites T-1-T-11). RV sites have water/electric/sewer, 20/30-amp, dump station; max trailer length 32 ft. Open ~late May (Memorial Day)-mid Oct (Columbus Day). Both nightly transient and seasonal sites; 2-night weekend minimum. Phone reservations only with mailed deposit check, no online booking. Store, laundry, heated restrooms/showers. --Claude

was: Family-owned campground on the Bearcamp River, 11 Jackman Pond Rd, South Tamworth; ~27-35 sites, a mix of seasonal and nightly. Full hookups (water/sewer, 20/30/50-amp) on pull-thrus and back-ins, plus partial-hookup sites for tents, vans and pop-ups; max RV ~45-60 ft. Pool, playground, store, bathhouse, riverwalk. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Book by phone. --Claude

was: Drive-to campground at the park's US 221 Access; the park's other campgrounds are walk-in or paddle-in only. Half the sites have full hookups. The dump station charges a fee. Vehicle GPS units misplace the park address: navigate to 36.46768,-81.34035 (the booking site's advice). --Claude

was: Moccasin Branch Campground (opened ~2023), at 814 Moccasin Branch Road just before the park's main entrance. The hookup sites have long driveways; the no-hookup sites are drive-to tent-and-trailer sites with large tent pads. 6 camper cabins. --Claude

was: Juniper Creek Outfitters campground on a 22-acre fishing lake (catch and release, no gas motors) near Chinquapin; the RV row has lake views, primitive tent sites sit across the dam, plus two cabins. Boat ramps, fishing, kayak/canoe rentals, trails. Instead of sewer hookups the owners pump out tanks from a mobile septic trailer. --Claude

was: Union County park on 350-acre Cane Creek Lake; the family camping area has easy access to the lake. Also walk-in wilderness tent sites, group sites and rustic cabins. --Claude

was: Two camping areas, one near the park entrance and one near the White Oaks picnic area. Roads narrow/steep. --Claude

was: Primitive USFS campground on Citico Creek, Cherokee NF (Tellico Ranger District). 7 sites, standard nonelectric -- no hookups, no potable water (bring your own), vault toilet. Each site has picnic table, fire ring/grill, lantern post. Firsthand report: gravel road passable by normal vehicles (no 4WD), sites fairly level, Site 2 best for RVs. Pay on-site by cash/check or Recreation.gov Scan-and-Pay QR. Open roughly March-November (2025: Mar 6-Nov 17). Max 5 people per site; horses not allowed. --Claude

was: Campground on TVA's Watts Bar Lake, family-owned since 2006 and a charter member of TVA's Camp-Right program, where every site is on or looks over the lake and has a fire pit with a grill and a picnic table.  Most sites have 50, 30 and 20 amps; 18 have only 30 and 20.  There are three bathhouses, a free dump station or a pump-out at the site ($30-45), a gated boat ramp, boat slips ($10 a night), two beaches, a camp store with live bait, laundry, propane, a playground, and kayaks, canoes, paddleboards and paddle boats to rent ($25-35 a day); Wi-Fi is at the office only.  Most of the campground closes in mid-November, but 25 sites stay open all year. --Claude
